item.title: Top 7 Ways to Disable Missing Docstring Warnings at a File-Level in Pylint
item.description:
Pylint often raises alerts when it detects that your code files are not following docstring practices. Sometimes, you might find yourself in a situation where you want to maintain internal documentation for classes and functions without the necessity of including a file-level docstring. Fortunately, there are several methods to configure Pylint to ignore these warnings while still keeping core linting features active. Here are the top seven techniques to achieve this customization.

### Method 1: Disable Specific Warnings

Instead of silencing all linting errors using the `--errors-only` flag, it is more efficient to specify which warnings to disable. The command format you would want to use is `--disable=<msg_ids>`.

For instance, to disable the warning identifying missing docstrings, which corresponds to message ID `C0111`, adjust your Pylint command as follows:

```bash
pylint --disable=C0111 your_file.py
